title: Floor shows, Dick Shawn, Russ Papalia and Billy DeWolf
summary: He tells of playing for Dick Shawn and others, using trombonist Russ Papalia as his substitute, and a joke from Billy DeWolf and a critic's review.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Pat Cooper played bass for him. At the Grand, he plays with the accordionist who also played with me at various times. Of course in my career of over 40 years as a leader I had a lot of different musicians, but always had the best I hope. Some of whom maybe were not considered the best by some other man leaders who were ignorant. They didn't know that you had to have a man who could play a floor show, you know? I played for Dick Shawn, I didn't know him for Madame, he throws me the books. I say Dick Shawn, well he'll phrase me, he'll do notes. He did it in about an hour and a half. I didn't rehearse him, 45 minutes. It would take Ed Sullivan all week to rehearse him. I played his show. He says I know you now, you're Johnny. I said how you know me? He says the spotlight man told me that you would have preached the trumpet at the Orpheus. I said you're going back in the prehistoric days. He says but that shows me that you have the experience. And I played his act and he just hugged me and I thanked him. I didn't ask for testimonials, I didn't hear the thing. But I know Dick Shawn, same way when I played the Four Freedoms Show, when they were selling bombs, they brought down that handsome fellow, who was that ladies man, that good looking actor, he's been years going by. And you see I'll tell you my memory goes back. Well I knew show better, so I played everything from the Monkeys to Grand Opera. And one show I had to lay off I sent Russ Papalia because Russ Papalia was my protege. Russ formerly played trombone in my band. And when I hired Russ he almost faded because it's your band. I said Russ you play a good solid trombone, you play the spots. And naturally being vain I didn't want any trombone to play a cover of me on people with
Well I was a leader. So I put Russ there, I went to show and I came back. Billy DeWolf, Billy DeWolf. You've heard of him?

I'll get the other fella's name, he was a ladies man from Taw, he was a handsome fellow, a leading man. And Billy DeWolf looks down at the pit and he tells that huge audience, I felt like a millionaire. He says it is certainly a pleasure to see Johnny Dread back in the pit. He missed me so much. Because his motions and his actions were strictly more of them. You know he's an old timer. They call him Mr. Billy DeWolf now. Well I mean all that makes you feel good. Like I can recite that writer where the man says, it was mighty nice to see Johnny back in the pit with his triumphant trumpet. That's a good word, that. Triumphant trumpet. And with that exception there was nothing of merit in his show. Now I'm sure they cost thousands of dollars. You think that I would, his son, Emel Washburn, he just loved me. He died. Have you heard of Emel Washburn? I've heard of him. I don't know. He was a theatrical writer. KTK, did you ever hear of him? He had acid on his tongue. They were all afraid of him. They were all afraid of him. And when they knew that KTK was in the front, I don't think they could do that. But what did New Orleans mean? They had a week in New Orleans and gone. But never had an acid touch for me. He said someday they're going to realize they got something. You know?
